title: Reduce observability hotpath syscalls and introduce lightweight probe shim
creator: Priya Patel
description: Problem: Production telemetry hotpaths are contributing measurable p99 tail latency and CPU spikes on busy runtime pods. Root causes identified in preliminary profiling: frequent small syscalls from the log/metric writer, unbatched OTLP exports for short-lived requests, and a synchronous sampling decision made inline with request handling. Goal: Reduce observability overhead on the runtime hotpath without losing actionable telemetry, provide an incremental migration path, and ensure rollbacks are safe.
work_summary:
Scope and acceptance criteria:
- Introduce a minimal "probe shim" that lives in-process and coalesces spans/metrics/logs to a memory ring buffer; background worker flushes to OTLP/gRPC exporter.
- Eliminate direct syscall-heavy paths from the hot request flow (target: 30-50% reduction in p99 extra CPU and wall-time per request on heavy workloads).
- Move sampling decision out of synchronous hotpath and support per-route dynamic sampling configs.
- Keep default behavior identical; feature behind a runtime flag and rollout policy.
- Provide benchmark harness and litmus tests for tail-latency, memory, and steady-state CPU.

Technical approach and trade-offs:
1) Probe shim implemented in Rust (FFI to existing runtime) to minimize allocations and rely on a lock-free ring buffer. Trade-offs: adds a small native binary and FFI surface but reduces Go/Python syscalls.
2) Background flush worker uses batched OTLP/gRPC with gzip compression when payloads > 32KB; fall back to protobuf over http only in legacy private deployments.
3) Sampling: introduce a single byte decision on hotpath with an async enrichment path that attaches full attributes after the fact for kept traces. This reduces per-request allocations at the cost of slightly delayed attribute availability in rare debug scenarios.
4) Fallback and safety: if ring buffer saturation detected, shim drops non-critical metric events and records a local metric that surfaces in the Console to avoid blocking requests.

Benchmarks and targets:
- Baseline: current p99 added latency = 18ms at 95% CPU load. Target p99 added latency <= 8ms.
- Memory: additional RSS per pod <= 24MB.
- CPU: steady-state CPU delta reduced by 35% at 10k rps synthetic load.

Acceptance criteria:
- Canary rollout on staging and two dedicated clusters with production-like traffic showing target improvements.
- No increase in trace/sample loss beyond an agreed threshold (<=1% additional loss for low-volume routes).
- Console exposes a new 'probe-health' dashboard and an alert if ring buffer overflow happens more than 1/minute for 5m.

Migration and rollout plan:
- Feature gated via runtime flag (observability.probe.enabled=false by default).
- Step 1: deploy to non-prod with flag on for 10% of pods, run benchmark harness.
- Step 2: expand to canary clusters, run traffic replay and monitor.
- Step 3: enable for Dedicated customers by request, maintain opt-out.
- Step 4: default enable after 8-week stabilization period with metrics review.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Probe+Shim+Design
- Benchmark harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-bench/tree/eng-214999
- Spike PR (prototype ring buffer): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4812
- Implementation PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4989

Notes about compatibility:
- For Private/VPC customers without gRPC egress we keep a small HTTP exporter bridge. This path will not have compression but still benefits from in-process batching.
- We will coordinate with SDK teams to ensure trace-context propagation remains unchanged.

2025-02-20 - Marcus Rey: Spike complete. Prototype shows 3x reduction in syscall frequency; p99 hotpath latency reduced from 18ms->9ms under synthetic load. Linked spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4812

2025-02-25 - QA (Chen Li): Running stress tests with 30m sustained traffic. Observed occasional ring buffer saturation under pathological bursts. Added a saturation metric and drop policy proposal to the design doc.

2025-02-27 - Design review (Ariel Kim): Agreed on Rust shim for low allocation path; requested a clear rollback playbook and a metric that surfaces any dropped telemetry in Console (ENG-214999 metric: probe.telemetry.dropped_count).

2025-03-02 - Marcus Rey: Initial implementation PR opened (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4989. Current status: core ring buffer, background flusher, and basic OTLP exporter wired. Failing tests: two integration tests around shutdown ordering. Investigating graceful drain sequence.
2025-03-04 - Priya Patel: Updated acceptance criteria to include 'no more than 1% additional trace loss' and added release gating steps. Scheduled canary window for 2025-03-18 in staging clusters.
